summary: Client cache of mod.io dependency lists, written by ls::ugc::ModDependencyCachedRequestSystem::Update: HashMap<ls::ugc::ModItemDependenciesInfoID, DynamicArray<net::UGCModDependency>> plus a DynamicArray<ModItemDependenciesInfoID> of pending ids at +0x40 (macOS destructor and Update). The map is written out member by member because its key is a struct (the build forbids own structs as hash keys). Live: idle, all zero.

fields.name: ModId
fields.evidence: ls::ugc::ModItemDependenciesInfoID: Windows bg3.exe+0x3BE4540 compares ids as '(*a == *b) && ((char)a[1] == (char)b[1])' (a qword and the byte at +8) and hashes them as '*id % bucket count'; keys/elements have a 16-byte stride. macOS ModDependencyCachedRequestSystemHelper::RequestItemDependencies(unsigned long long, bool): the 64-bit mod item id.

fields.name: field_8
fields.evidence: The byte compared at +8 (Windows bg3.exe+0x3BE4540): the bool argument of RequestItemDependencies(unsigned long long, bool) on macOS; meaning not established.

fields.name: HashKeys
fields.evidence: Bucket table of the ls::HashMap<ls::ugc::ModItemDependenciesInfoID, ls::ugc::ModItemDependenciesInfoResponse> (macOS ~HashMap of that type); creator bg3.exe+0x3BE5780 zeroes 0x50 bytes; destructor bg3.exe+0x3B79D60 ends with the plain-key HashSet destructor bg3.exe+0x582AD0 on +0. Written member by member because the key is a struct.

fields.name: NextIds
fields.evidence: Hash chain array of the ls::HashTable (int32 links).

fields.name: Keys
fields.evidence: Key array: Windows bg3.exe+0x3BE4540 compares '*(map[4] + idx*0x10)' and the byte at +8 with an id, key count at +0x2C.

fields.name: Values
fields.evidence: Value storage, one ls::ugc::ModItemDependenciesInfoResponse per key, 0x20-byte stride (Windows): destructor helper bg3.exe+0x3B7D760 clears the DynamicArray at value+8 of every value (i < key count +0x2C, stride 0x20) with bg3.exe+0x38BB690; bg3.exe+0x3BE4540 / +0x3BE5100 copy a value as qword +0, DynamicArray +8, byte +0x18. Response layout (Windows): +0 uint64 (not named), +8 DynamicArray<net::UGCModDependency> (0x50-byte elements: uint64 + three 24-byte STDStrings, element destructor bg3.exe+0x38BC7A0; macOS AppendEmplace<unsigned long long, char const*, STDString const&, STDString const&>), +0x18 bool, 7 bytes padding. Spelled out as raw parts (a struct key forbids the HashMap form).

fields.name: RecentIds
fields.evidence: Windows bg3.exe+0x3BE4540: after a response is cached, the id is looked up in the 16-byte-stride array at +0x40 (count +0x4C, compares qword and byte) and moved (bg3.exe+0x3BE5650) or appended (bg3.exe+0x3BE5480); then 'while (count > 15)' the array's entry is popped and removed from the map - an LRU list that caps the cache at 16 entries. Destructor frees it as a plain array (bg3.exe+0x5BD630).

open_questions: Meaning of ModItemDependenciesInfoID +8 (bool) and of the response's +0 qword / +0x18 byte (value struct is spelled as raw parts anyway).
Which end of RecentIds is the oldest entry.
second_pass: Settled on Windows: bg3.exe+0x3BE4540 shows the 16-byte key (qword + byte compared, qword hashed), the 0x20-byte values and the +0x40 LRU array capped at 16; the destructor bg3.exe+0x3B79D60/+0x3B7D760 confirms the value stride. macOS's 16-byte value guess was wrong: the value is a 0x20-byte ModItemDependenciesInfoResponse.
